name: Nextcloud
description: Nextcloud OCS API: users, groups, file shares, app capabilities and server status on your own Nextcloud. Basic auth with an app password, the OCS-APIRequest header and format=json.
instructions:
**Use an app password, never the account password.**
1. Sign in to Nextcloud and open **Settings → Security → Devices & sessions**.
2. Create a new app password named e.g. `AnythingMCP`. Nextcloud shows it once.
3. Set `NEXTCLOUD_URL` to your instance root (no trailing slash), `NEXTCLOUD_USERNAME` to the login name and `NEXTCLOUD_APP_PASSWORD` to the generated value. An app password can be revoked on its own, and it sidesteps two-factor authentication, which would otherwise break API access entirely.

**Three things every OCS call needs**, all of which this adapter sends for you:
- `Authorization: Basic …` from the username and app password,
- the `OCS-APIRequest: true` header — without it Nextcloud answers with an HTML login page and a 200, which looks like success and parses like nonsense,
- `format=json`, or the response comes back as XML.

**Two OCS versions live side by side.** The provisioning API (users, groups) is on `ocs/v1.php`; the sharing API is on `ocs/v2.php`. They also report errors differently — v1 puts the real status in the body's `meta.statuscode` while returning HTTP 200. Read `ocs.meta` before trusting `ocs.data`.

**Admin-only endpoints.** Listing users and groups requires an administrator or a group admin. A normal user's app password gets an OCS 997 (unauthorised) inside an HTTP 200.

**Files themselves are WebDAV, not OCS**, and are out of scope here: this connector manages users, groups and shares, not file contents.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch.
- On an internal host (`cloud.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

**Writes**: `nextcloud_create_share` publishes a real share. A public link share (`shareType: 3`) is reachable by anyone who has the URL — set a password and an expiry date unless you mean it to be open.

tools.name: nextcloud_get_capabilities
tools.description: Read the server's capabilities: Nextcloud version, enabled apps and their feature flags. Works for any authenticated user — the quickest proof the app password is accepted.

tools.name: nextcloud_get_user_status
tools.description: Read the status of the account the app password belongs to: quota, used space, display name, e-mail, groups and last login.

tools.name: nextcloud_list_users
tools.description: List user ids on the instance, optionally filtered by a search fragment. Requires an administrator or group-admin account.

search.description: Fragment matched against user id and display name.

tools.name: nextcloud_get_user
tools.description: Read one user's details: display name, e-mail, quota, group memberships, last login and whether the account is enabled. Admin only.

tools.name: nextcloud_list_groups
tools.description: List the groups defined on the instance, optionally filtered by a search fragment. Requires an administrator account.

search.description: Fragment matched against the group id.

tools.name: nextcloud_list_group_members
tools.description: List the user ids in one group — who actually has access to whatever is shared with that group.

tools.name: nextcloud_list_shares
tools.description: List shares the account owns or received, with their type, recipient, permissions, expiry and public link URL.

path.description: Restrict to shares of one path, relative to the user's files root, e.g. /Projects/Acme.

reshares.description: When true, include shares made by other users of the same file.

shared_with_me.description: When true, list shares received rather than shares made.

subfiles.description: When true and path is a folder, list shares of its children.

tools.name: nextcloud_get_share
tools.description: Read one share by its id: exactly who it is shared with, at what permission level, and when it expires.

tools.name: nextcloud_create_share
tools.description: Create a share. shareType 0 shares with a user, 1 with a group and 3 creates a public link that anyone with the URL can open — set a password and expireDate for those.

path.description: Path to share, relative to the user's files root, e.g. /Projects/Acme.

shareType.description: 0 user, 1 group, 3 public link, 4 e-mail, 6 federated cloud.

shareWith.description: User id, group id or e-mail address. Omit for a public link.

permissions.description: Bitmask: 1 read, 2 update, 4 create, 8 delete, 16 share. 1 for read-only.
